OUTPUT: one flat 1536x1024 texture sheet on uniform #101010 background. Exactly TWO straight rectangular horizontal wooden rails, each x64..1472 and 286px high: first y128..414, second y608..894. Orthographic front-facing elevation, no perspective. Each rail is a continuous single piece of wood with a straight thin lit upper bevel and straight dark lower bevel, no endcaps. Fill the entire rectangle with material. They are quiet structural rails, no ornaments. Continuous equal cross-section along their whole length. Long axis left to right, narrow bevel at top, darker thin bevel at bottom. The upper rail and lower rail have different natural grain patterns.

CRITICAL ART DIRECTION: sharply resolved organic LONGITUDINAL WOOD GRAIN, like high-quality hand-painted game prop texturing viewed close up. Within the wood face draw 15–25 thin flowing lengthwise fibre ridges at distinct heights; gently meandering but predominantly parallel. Mix slender dark hairline splits with narrow warm reflected-light lips, tapering incised pores and a few restrained shallow scratches. Grain features should occupy about 4–9 SOURCE px across, with gaps about 8–16 SOURCE px, so after reduction to 52px thickness they still read clearly as wood. Combine long fibres with short tapering interruptions, not horizontal ruler lines. This is smooth worked timber carrying fine grain, NOT tree bark, corrugated metal, ragged boards, peeling paint or grooves machined into a repeating pattern. Small dark pores, fine crisp fibres, tactile shallow relief; no broad blurred brown smears, no large smooth polygon patches. Coherent flowing grain must be the main visible improvement. Preserve the brown-red walnut hue; no orange, pale oak, yellow pine or glossy varnish. No noise spray or sharpening halos masquerading as fibre detail.

Lighting and repeat safety: consistent gentle top/front light and deep fine-fibre occlusion; no bright spot, lengthwise gradient, distinctive large knots or repeating stamp. The material must have a visually even brightness from left to right. Matching cross-sectional depth and similar grain density at both ends for seamless extension. Crisp straight horizontal contours and absolutely uniform thickness. No nails, brass, metal, joints, joinery notches, medallions, carved symbols, screws, text, captions, UI, trees, additional rectangles or complete frame.

This is local structural-run authoring, so the full-frame opening language below does NOT request a complete frame here. Apply its physical material, stable contour and neutral repeat requirements ONLY to these two rectangular rails. Existing alpha/opening/corners/ornaments will be preserved separately.

ACTUAL IMAGE-STAGE GUIDANCE:
# Image-stage frame construction contract

This is the image-model-facing projection of the parent skill and quality gates. Pass this text and `gothic-philosophy.md` as actual image-generation subject content, not merely to an intermediary model. Generalize the principles; the selected design basis owns style and motifs. Generate a new artwork when requested, never reuse a rejected frame as the finished result.

Design an adaptable crafted object around one strictly rectangular, uniformly coloured opening. The solid inner material contour touches that opening on all four sides. No picture mat, second inner frame, flat backing strip, empty moat, shadow sheet or translucent bridge between ornament and opening. Thickness is actual modelled material with bevels and recesses, not an enlarged canvas or a blank border. No faces, anatomy, text, UI or terminal screenshot.

Compose a few distinctive sculptural concentrations linked by genuinely quiet structural spans. Every side must contain a substantial straight, longitudinally uniform span, around 180–256 source pixels long on the requested 1536×1024 canvas, suitable for extending that side without changing its cross-sectional profile. Preserve a steady inner AND outer contour, material thickness and lighting along these spans. They are structural craftsmanship, not featureless background liners: model the cross-sectional relief and keep its longitudinal profile stable. Broad ornament can live outside these spans. A long diagonal, waving ribbon, taper, bead, gem, sparkle, leaf or repeated distinctive carving is not a neutral span.

Quiet spans meet adjacent fixed art with matching profile, tangent, relief and light. Do not ask later slicing to manufacture missing transitions. Do not use lighting gradients along these spans which turn into periodic pulses when repeated. Detail remains rich at the chosen focal objects; the linking material stays restrained. Corners and focal art retain natural proportions. Outer silhouette can rise and vary away from the quiet spans; the protected inner boundary remains uninterrupted.

The downstream assembler measures this actual opening, preserves the complete one-shot band artwork on either side of each selected quiet span, and repeats only the neutral span directly. It does not mirror curved art, synthesize a background, move the aperture to fit ornaments, or stretch a tiny sculpture fragment to arbitrary length. Generate material that is compatible with that construction. A complete raster should also read coherently before decomposition.

The deliverable is static frame art. No global glow pulses, motion blur, motion sequences or invented window shader. Any depicted local light should have a visible object/material cause. The owner's explicit design basis overrides borrowed Gothic vocabulary, not the geometric safety requirements.

## A-tier reference: Frieren Pearl Mixed

The owner rated Gothic Eclipse S-tier and the latest Frieren Pearl Mixed A-tier after its live preview. These are artistic reference grades, not automated scores or proof that every size/animation phase is defect-free. Aim for a coherent, usable A-tier candidate; do not promise S-tier, self-award owner acceptance, or enter an unrequested endless refinement loop.

Frieren's new design is jewellery-like rather than Gothic masonry: pale silver with restrained warm rose reflections, readable bevelled rails, four pearlescent corner bodies, sculpted leaf clusters, small red gem settings, delicate bead pendants and four midpoint star ornaments. Hierarchy: corner clusters first, midpoint stars second, calm rails third. Retain material colour, luminous pearl volume and dark carved recesses; do not flatten everything into white silhouettes, global glow or a uniform palette tint. This motif set describes this reference only: another wallpaper keeps its own design language and need not acquire pearls, leaves, red gems, symmetry or exactly four stars.

The manual repair separated stationary supporting rails from one-shot sculpture. Transfer the visual principle: quiet, straight supporting material reaches the client boundary; elaborate objects remain complete and naturally proportioned, with enough outward room for their silhouettes. Midpoint ornaments must be visible over their supporting rail, not moved into the opening or into empty exterior margin. Their roots share the rail's relief and illumination. Do not depend on later masks to invent missing attachments, recover clipped tips or hide seams.

## Motion-ready art, without pretending to output an animation

When the brief explicitly requests later object animation, still deliver the single static master required by this stage. Make leaf clusters legible as coherent articulated groups with identifiable attachment roots. Keep fixed gems, settings, rails and hanging chains visually separable from moving foliage; avoid interweaving a wire through every leaf or fusing all objects into one inseparable mass. Pearl bodies need a readable complete volume and an attachment/setting; do not paint motion trails, multiple phases, detached flying leaves or pre-rendered droplets into the master.

Allow outward room around moving objects while preserving the protected rectangular opening and neutral runs. Composition must look intentional at rest, not like an exploded asset sheet. Only a later supported layer-authoring stage may produce background, petal masks, pearl bodies, sockets and foreground occluders. This image call cannot create those files by implication, and the current Studio button does not automatically author Frieren's mixed effect. Return only this stage's existing output format; no invented manifest keys or extra tool calls.


ACTUAL AUTHORED CONSTRUCTION PHILOSOPHY:
# Gothic Eclipse: reusable design philosophy

Version: 2026-10-02. This is an authored interpretation of the accepted Gothic Eclipse frame, not a new model analysis and not a command to make every frame gothic. Evidence: the four sessions and explicit owner acceptance in `session-lessons.md`; one direct inspection of `assets/source/gothic_eclipse_minimal_idle_2x.png`. Refresh only when the reference or owner's decisions change. Do not reattach or reanalyze that image on every generation.

## Transfer the construction, not the props

Gothic reads as an assembled physical object, not a rectangular background carrying stickers. Pillars support a lintel; footings carry weight; carved brackets turn corners; ornaments grow out of that construction. The source uses weathered dark stone, small warm fissures, an eclipse crest and candles. Those are its vocabulary, not universal requirements. In quality mode translate the construction into the requested material family (silverwork, wood, botanical carving, ceramic, etc.); do not import stone, skulls, flames or cathedral tracery unless that design actually calls for them. In explicit gothic mode retain the architectural vocabulary as described here; no image attachment is needed to recover it.

## Hierarchy and asymmetry

The broad structural silhouette reads first, medium relief second, tiny cuts and texture third. A large top crest, smaller architectural breaks, unequal corners and the lower-left candle cluster create hierarchy; long quieter spans prevent detail from becoming noise. Their exact placement is not a mandatory template. Use a few intentional concentrations of detail joined by restrained construction. Do not spread identical ornaments at regular intervals simply because a layout can tile them. Richness comes from designed form and material depth, not object count.

## Depth belongs to the material

Faces, bevels, recessed channels, occlusion and consistent highlights establish thickness. Dark recesses remain part of the material; they are not a separate broad black liner between decoration and content. Light has a local cause and reveals the relief; it does not wash the whole frame or the opening. In a pale-metal frame, differentiated edge highlights and recesses can do the same work without borrowing Gothic's orange light.

## Content is an opening, not a picture mounted on a mat

The terminal occupies the actual opening in the object. The material's inner edge meets its rectangular boundary directly. There is no second inner rectangle, moat, picture-frame mat, flat backing strip or translucent bridge. Exterior silhouette may be irregular and airy; the inner material boundary is continuous and protects the content. If an ornament needs space, recompose or thicken its supporting material, not the gap. Source aperture, material contour and reserved screen space are separate measurements.

## Adaptability is part of the drawing

Unique architecture retains its shape. Flexible length lives in deliberately calm structural runs whose cross-section, contour and lighting remain stable along their axis. A straight carved shaft can supply extra length; a sloping ribbon, star, gem or bulging scroll cannot. Transitions into a flexible run must already share its profile and tangent. Repetition must not produce a zigzag, a ladder of ornaments or periodic lighting pulses. Matching endpoint pixels alone does not establish a sound join. Preserve every meaningful object once; do not cover duplicate copies with an opaque patch.

## Motion continues an object

The accepted Gothic motion was flame around an existing wick and wax passing behind existing stone. It was not global breathing opacity. Static is the default for a new frame; animation and whole-window shaders are separate design decisions, not a way to rescue poor geometry.

## What success means

At ordinary working scale the frame should read as one crafted object touching the terminal, with clear material depth and a controlled focal hierarchy. Resizing changes calm span lengths, not sculpture proportions. A clear centre, an accepted manifest or a successful image call is not visual acceptance. Owner rejection remains authoritative.
